{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''William Frank Brinkman''' is an American physicist who served as president of the [[American Physical Society]] (2002)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brinkman Looks Back on Good Science and Tough Decisions|url=http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201305/brinkman.cfm|access-date=2021-09-28|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> and was the head of the [[Office of Science]] at the [[United States Department of Energy]] (2009–2013). He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1984, and won the [[George E. Pake Prize]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|title=George E. Pake Prize|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/pake.cfm|access-date=2021-09-28|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> He was elected as a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1992,<ref>{{Cite web|title=William Frank Brinkman|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/william-frank-brinkman|access-date=2021-03-23|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> and became a member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=William+F.+Brinkman&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-09-28|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>

Brinkman was born on July 20, 1938, in [[Washington, Missouri]]. He received his bachelor's degree (1960) and PhD (1965) in physics from the [[University of Missouri]].<ref name="aip">{{cite web |title=Brinkman, William F. |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11412021.html |website=history.aip.org |publisher=American Institute of Physics |access-date=21 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Godwin |first1=Linda |title=Bill Brinkman Selected for Inaugural Alumni Award |url=https://physics.missouri.edu/sites/default/files/basic-files/physicsnewsletter2017.pdf |work=Physics and Astronomy Communiqué |publisher=University of Missouri |date=Autumn 2017}}</ref>

Brinkman joined [[Bell Labs]] in 1966, working in the physics research laboratory. From 1984 to 1987, he served as vice president of research at [[Sandia National Laboratories]]. In 1987 he became executive director of the physics research division at Bell Labs.<ref name="aip"/>

Brinkman joined [[Princeton University]] in 2001, where he continued his [[condensed matter physics]] research. In 2009, he was appointed as director of the Office of Science in the U.S. Department of Energy, where he served until 2013.<ref>{{cite web |last1=MacPherson |first1=Kitta |title=Brinkman confirmed as director of DOE's Office of Science |url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2009/06/23/brinkman-confirmed-director-does-office-science |website=Princeton University |language=en |date=June 23, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=William Brinkman |url=https://www.energy.gov/contributors/william-brinkman |website=Energy.gov |publisher=U.S. Department of Energy |language=en |date=March 24, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Service |first1=Robert F. |last2=Malakoff |first2=David |title=DOE Science Chief to Step Down |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/doe-science-chief-step-down |work=Science |publisher=AAAS |date=20 March 2013 |language=en}}</ref>
